engagement_background.objective: Leverage Epika’s total buying power to capture $0.7-1.6M+ in annual cost savings (and corresponding enterprise-value uplift) through a 6-month strategic-sourcing program while laying the foundation for a best-in-class, enterprise-wide procurement process.
engagement_background.scope_summary: 13 direct and indirect spend categories representing $51.9 M in total spend and $36.2 M of addressable spend were placed in scope, including OEM parts, aftermarket parts, oil/lubricants, filters, employee benefits, P-Card spend, fuel, telecom, GIS/MRO, tires, uniforms, waste and office supplies. Tail spend within each category and very low-value categories may be dropped if savings are immaterial.
constraints_challenges: Eight business units purchase independently, creating a highly decentralized supplier landscape that must be unified for enterprise negotiations.
Historical line-item usage data is incomplete; Treya must request data directly from key suppliers to build baselines.
Some incumbent suppliers are considered strategic, leading to potential push-back and the need for a ‘united front’ and sensitive negotiation approach.
Risk of parallel/unsanctioned sourcing conversations by Epika staff could confuse the market; project success requires tight control of supplier communications.
Aggressive timeline—savings targeted by February 2025 to support private-equity value-creation and pending transaction milestones.

procurement_environment.data_availability: AP/PO data exists within each business unit, but consolidated spend visibility is limited; detailed SKU-level usage often must be sourced from suppliers; contracts are dispersed across units.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Multiple BU systems and naming conventions; gaps in historical usage when suppliers do not respond; no central contract repository.
